The '''1760 [[FLLA]] World Cup''' was the 23rd edition of the [[FLLA World Cup]], the quadrennial international [[Arraby]] tournament contested by the senior men's national teams of the member associations of the [[FLLA]]. It was held in [[Ukhdari]] from 11 June to 11 July 1760, after the country had been awarded hosting rights by the [[FLLA]] Council on 4 February 1754. It was the first FLLA World Cup ever staged in [[Ukhdari]], and the first to be held anywhere in [[Ayuma]] since the [[1744 FLLA World Cup|1744 edition]] in [[Lycroa]]. Thirty-two nations qualified for the final tournament, drawn from the seven continental confederations of the [[FLLA]], and contested 64 matches across ten host venues.

[[Verusa]] won the tournament, defeating [[Raledria]] 2–1 in the [[#Final|final]] to claim their second FLLA World Cup title.<ref name="flla-final">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/final-report|title=Verusa win 1760 FLLA World Cup with 2–1 final victory over Raledria|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=11 July 1760}}</ref> Verusa reached the final despite finishing second in Group F behind [[Taval]], to whom they had lost their opening group fixture; they then won all four of their knockout matches, eliminating the hosts [[Ukhdari]], [[Ohtina]], [[Ztesh]] and finally Raledria without conceding more than a single goal in any of them. [[Ztesh]] finished third, defeating [[Haiza]] 1–0 in the third-place playoff. The hosts, Ukhdari, won Group F with a perfect record but were eliminated in the round of sixteen by the eventual champions Verusa, losing 1–0 at the Stadion Faramozan.

A total of 183 goals were scored in 64 matches at an average of 2.86 per match.<ref name="flla-stats">{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/tournament-statistics|title=1760 FLLA World Cup: final tournament statistics|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=18 August 1760}}</ref> [[Trian]] finished as the tournament's leading goalscoring nation with 12 goals, despite being eliminated in the quarter-finals, and Trian forward Aldan Verric was awarded the FLLA Marskval as the tournament's top individual scorer with seven goals. The Best Player award (the FLLA Vairan Ball) was given to Verusan central midfielder Halo Markenrick, who captained the champions throughout the tournament. The round of sixteen was unusually disruptive: only three of the eight group winners reached the quarter-finals, with five group runners-up eliminating the side that had topped their group.

==Host selection==
{{Main|1760 FLLA World Cup bids}}

[[Ukhdari]] was confirmed as the host of the 1760 FLLA World Cup by the [[FLLA]] Council on 4 February 1754, ending a bidding process that had opened twenty-two months earlier. The Ukhdari Arraby Association's bid, formally submitted in August 1751, prevailed over rival proposals from [[Praesyu]] and [[Estijan]]; a fourth bid from [[Easuhura]] had been withdrawn at the longlist stage in October 1752 on grounds related to the planned reconstruction of two principal venues.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/news/1754/host-selection-ukhdari|title=Ukhdari confirmed as 1760 hosts|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=4 February 1754}}</ref>

In its bid, the Ukhdari Arraby Association proposed a programme of stadium construction and renovation across nine cities, four of which had not previously hosted senior international Arraby. The total infrastructure budget pledged by the Ukhdari federal government and participating municipalities was {{lahn}}1.7&nbsp;billion, of which {{lahn}}480&nbsp;million was directed towards public-transport upgrades in the host cities. A separate operational budget of {{lahn}}280&nbsp;million was allocated to security, broadcasting infrastructure and the volunteer programme.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uaa.org.ukh/1751/world-cup-bid-dossier|title=Ukhdari 1760 FLLA World Cup bid dossier|publisher=Ukhdari Arraby Association|date=12 August 1751}}</ref>

==Participating teams and officials==

===Qualification===
{{Main|1760 FLLA World Cup qualification}}
[[File:1760 FLLA World Cup qualification.png|thumb|upright=1.5|{{legend|#000cff|Countries qualified for World Cup}} {{legend|#ffb400|Country did not qualify}} {{legend|black|Countries that did not enter the World Cup or were expelled from the tournament by FLLA prior to playing a match}} {{legend|#ababab|Country not a FLLA member}}]]

A total of 32 places at the tournament were allocated across the seven continental confederations of the [[FLLA]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/qualification-allocation|title=Confederation berth allocation for the 1760 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=18 March 1757}}</ref> Each confederation administered its own qualifying competition, with the format reflecting the size of its membership and its allocation of finals berths. [[Ukhdari]] qualified as of right under FLLA hosting regulations and additionally took part in the [[AYFVL]] qualifying tournament in a non-binding capacity, finishing first in qualifying group B. The reigning champions [[Quidic]], winners of the [[1756 FLLA World Cup]], qualified through the [[QUFVL]] qualifiers.

The qualifying tournaments are summarised below; full results are recorded on the individual confederation pages.

===Final draw===
{{Main|1760 FLLA World Cup seeding}}

The final draw for the group stage was held at the National Cultural Centre in [[Faramozan]] on 2 December 1759, nine months before the opening match. The 32 qualified teams were divided into four pots of eight on the basis of their pre-tournament [[FLLA]] rankings, with the eight highest-ranked sides placed in the seeded pot. [[Ukhdari]] occupied a seeded position as hosts, alongside [[Raledria]], [[Verusa]], [[United Delet]], [[Quidic]], [[Praesyu]], [[Ztesh]] and [[Siana]]. The three remaining pots were arranged on geographical lines so as to maximise the continental diversity of each group, under the procedure approved by the FLLA Organising Committee in September 1759.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/final-draw|title=Procedures for the 1760 FLLA World Cup final draw|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=15 September 1759}}</ref>

The draw was conducted by FLLA general secretary Yorvan Lestrika and presented by Ukhdari broadcaster Ranev Olsava, with retired internationals from each of the seven confederations drawing the team names. The ceremony was televised by 38 broadcasters across more than 150 countries.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1759/final-draw-faramozan|title=1760 FLLA World Cup final draw held in Faramozan|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=2 December 1759}}</ref>

===Officials===
{{Main|1760 FLLA World Cup officials}}

The FLLA Referees Committee appointed 22 refereeing trios, each consisting of one referee and two assistants from the same national association, and four support pairs drawn from 18 nations between them. The selections were announced in two tranches between September 1759 and January 1760, following an assessment programme at the [[1759 FLLA Continental Champions Cup]] and at senior friendlies organised in [[Faramozan]] and [[Veshgadar]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/officials-announced|title=Match officials confirmed for the 1760 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=20 January 1760}}</ref>

The opening match was refereed by Itsuki Kayama of [[Ztesh]], a [[QUFVL]]-affiliated official, the first time a [[QUFVL]] referee had taken charge of a World Cup opening fixture. The final was officiated by Brennan Quill of [[New Misos]], a [[ATFVL]]-affiliated official. The two semi-finals were taken by Lassan Vetren of [[Walporein]] ([[NAFVL]]) for the first semi-final and Ekho Marsuun of [[Pelugrotoa]] ([[MAFVL]]) for the second. The 22 selected referees were drawn from 18 nations and represented all seven [[FLLA]] confederations.

==Squads==
{{Main|1760 FLLA World Cup squads}}

The 1760 edition was the first FLLA World Cup at which each participating squad was required to consist of 23 players, three of whom had to be goalkeepers, replacing the previous 22-player allocation in force since 1740. Each participating national association was required to confirm its final 23-player squad with the FLLA no later than 10 days before the opening match; late replacements were permitted in the event of serious injury at any time up to 24 hours before a team's first fixture. A total of 736 players were registered for the tournament, of whom 96 were goalkeepers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/squad-lists-confirmed|title=Final 23-player squad lists confirmed for the 1760 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=1 June 1760}}</ref> The 23-player squad rule was retained at the [[1764 FLLA World Cup|subsequent edition]] and at every FLLA World Cup since.

The oldest player at the tournament was [[Etirha|Etirhan]] central defender Halric Sorne, who was 36 years and 224 days old at the start of the competition; the youngest was [[Verusa|Verusan]] forward Devan Lehrek (19 years and 53 days), who would go on to win the [[#Awards|Best Young Player]] award.<ref name="flla-stats" /> The mean age of registered players across the tournament was 27.1 years.

==Venues==
{{Main|1760 FLLA World Cup venues}}

Ten stadiums in nine host cities were used in the final tournament, with all venues located in [[Ukhdari]].<ref name="uaa-venues">{{cite web|url=https://www.uaa.org.ukh/1760/host-venues|title=Host venues of the 1760 FLLA World Cup|publisher=Ukhdari Arraby Association|date=3 March 1760}}</ref> Six of the ten venues had been built specifically for the tournament or substantially redeveloped during the bidding period; the remaining four, comprising the Stadion Faramozan, the Veshgadar Olympic Stadium, the Borshavi National Park Stadium and Asuna Field, were existing top-flight venues that received targeted upgrades to seating and broadcasting facilities.

The opening match was held at the 92,000-seat Stadion Faramozan in the capital, which also staged the final on 11 July; with eight matches in total it was one of the principal venues of the tournament, alongside the Veshgadar Olympic Stadium and Asuna Field. The two semi-finals were divided between the Veshgadar Olympic Stadium and the Borshavi National Park Stadium. The third-place playoff was held at the Dy Sports Complex.

===Team base camps===

Each of the 32 participating squads selected a base camp in Ukhdari from a shortlist of 76 candidate sites circulated by the host association in October 1759. Most teams opted for camps in or around the larger southern host cities, with eleven squads basing themselves within a one-hour radius of [[Veshgadar]] and a further eight in the [[Veshgadar metropolitan area]].

==Innovations==

The 1760 FLLA World Cup introduced a number of regulatory and presentational changes. The 23-player squad rule, replacing the 22-player allocation in force since 1740, was the most significant of these; the rule required each association to register exactly twenty-three players, including three goalkeepers, no later than 10 days before the opening fixture. The competition was also the first at which substitution requests were required to be submitted to the fourth official on a standardised written slip, a procedural change adopted by the FLLA Council on 11 March 1759 to reduce dispute on the touchline. A third change, the allocation of one additional pre-match warm-up period in cooler outdoor conditions, was incorporated at the request of the Ukhdari Arraby Association in March 1760.

==Format==

The 32 qualified teams were divided into eight groups of four for the group stage, drawn at the [[#Final draw|final draw]] on 2 December 1759. Each group operated on a single round-robin basis, with each team playing three matches; teams were awarded three points for a win, one for a draw and none for a defeat. The top two teams from each group advanced to the [[#Knockout stage|knockout stage]] while the bottom two were eliminated. Tiebreakers between teams level on points were applied in the following order: overall goal difference, overall goals scored, head-to-head record, fair-play points, and, if necessary, a drawing of lots by the FLLA Organising Committee.

In the knockout stage, fixtures were single-elimination ties played over 90 minutes; ties level at the end of normal time were extended by a single 30-minute period of [[wikipedia:Extra time|extra time]] of two 15-minute halves, with a [[wikipedia:Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] used to decide ties that remained level after extra time. Both the semi-final losers contested a [[#Third place playoff|third-place playoff]] on 10 July 1760.

==Opening ceremony==

The opening ceremony of the 1760 FLLA World Cup was held at the Stadion Faramozan on 11 June 1760, seventy-five minutes before the kick-off of the opening match between [[Ukhdari]] and [[Acetoa]]. Directed by Ukhdari stage producer Vasik Tolan and choreographed by Inara Mavzhi, the ceremony lasted 26 minutes and featured 1,050 dancers, 220 musicians and a flyover by the Ukhdari Air Force display team. The performance opened with a representation of the seven continental confederations of the [[FLLA]], each portrayed in costume and movement evoking the geography of its host continent, before transitioning to a sequence inspired by the founding of the Ukhdari federation. The Ukhdari vocalist Sava Reldan, joined by the Faramozan Symphony, performed the tournament's official theme song "One Field, One Game" as the closing item of the ceremony.

Attending dignitaries included the Ukhdari High Minister, the President of the FLLA Council, the heads of state of [[Verusa]], [[Praesyu]] and [[Siana]], and 76 ambassadors and senior diplomatic representatives. The ceremony was watched by an estimated worldwide television audience of 3.1 billion people.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/opening-ceremony|title=1760 FLLA World Cup opening ceremony staged in Faramozan|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=11 June 1760}}</ref>

==Group stage==

The 32 qualified teams were drawn into eight groups of four. Each group operated on a single round-robin basis, with each team playing three matches; the top two finishers in each group advanced to the [[#Knockout stage|knockout stage]] while the bottom two were eliminated. Group rankings were settled first on points (three for a win, one for a draw), then on goal difference and goals scored.

The group stage produced four perfect records: [[United Delet]] in Group B, [[Siana]] in Group D, [[Taval]] in Group E and the hosts [[Ukhdari]] in Group F all took maximum points from their three matches. The biggest win of the round was [[Trian]]'s 6–0 defeat of [[Astye]] in Group B, while several groups produced seven-goal contests, including [[Pelines]] 4–3 [[Astye]] and [[Quidic]] 3–4 [[Isari]]. The FLLA identified [[Kusierna]]'s 3–2 victory over [[Praesyu]] in Group A, achieved against a side ranked 206 places higher, as the tournament's biggest pre-tournament-ranking upset.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/group-stage-review|title=1760 FLLA World Cup group stage review|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=27 June 1760}}</ref>

All times listed are Standard Ukhdari Time ([[wikipedia:UTC+01:00|SUT]], [[wikipedia:UTC|UTC]]+1).

==Knockout stage==

The knockout stage involved the sixteen teams that advanced from the group stage. Matches still level after 90 minutes were extended by a 30-minute period of [[wikipedia:Extra time|extra time]]; if scores remained tied after extra time, the tie was decided by [[wikipedia:Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]]. Four of the eight round-of-sixteen ties and one of the four quarter-finals required additional time; the round-of-sixteen tie between [[Raledria]] and [[Dahe]] was decided 10–9 on penalties, the longest shoot-out in FLLA World Cup history.

===Round of 16===

The eight group winners were drawn against the eight group runners-up, with each match-up pairing teams from different groups. The round proved unusually disruptive, with five of the eight group winners eliminated, including four of the four sides that had won their group with a perfect record. The hosts [[Ukhdari]] were beaten 1–0 by the eventual champions [[Verusa]] in front of an 89,100 crowd at the Stadion Faramozan, becoming the third FLLA host nation in the past five editions to be eliminated before the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/round-of-16-report|title=Verusa end Ukhdari's home World Cup in the round of 16|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=1 July 1760}}</ref> [[Raledria]] and [[Dahe]] played out a goalless tie settled only after 22 penalty kicks, Raledria prevailing 10–9.

===Quarter-finals===

Three of the four quarter-finals were decided in normal time, with [[Ztesh]] again advancing on penalties after a 1–1 draw with [[Praesyu]]. [[Raledria]] produced the most emphatic result of the round, defeating Group E winners [[Taval]] 3–1 at the Veshgadar Olympic Stadium, while [[Haiza]] came from behind to beat [[Trian]] 3–2 and [[Verusa]] edged [[Ohtina]] 1–0 at the Borshavi National Park Stadium.

===Semi-finals===

The first semi-final was settled inside 90 minutes: [[Raledria]] came from behind to beat [[Haiza]] 2–1 at the Veshgadar Olympic Stadium, forward Niall Brask scoring the winner with twelve minutes remaining. In the second semi-final [[Verusa]] beat [[Ztesh]] 2–0 at the Borshavi National Park Stadium, through goals from Tovan Brunscar and the 19-year-old Devan Lehrek, to reach their second FLLA World Cup final.

===Third place playoff===

The third-place playoff was contested between the two losing semi-finalists at the Dy Sports Complex on 10 July. [[Ztesh]] won 1–0 through a 54th-minute strike from midfielder Sota Renji, securing the highest FLLA World Cup finish in the country's history and a third-place medal for a [[QUFVL]] nation for the first time since the confederation's reorganisation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/third-place-playoff|title=Ztesh take third place with win over Haiza in Dy|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=10 July 1760}}</ref>

===Final===
{{Main|1760 FLLA World Cup final}}

The final was contested between [[Verusa]] and [[Raledria]], the Group E runners-up and Group G winners respectively. Verusa won the match 2–1 to claim their second FLLA World Cup, having lost only once across the tournament, their opening group fixture against [[Taval]]. Verusan forward Tovan Brunscar opened the scoring in the 38th minute with a low drive from the edge of the penalty area; Raledrian forward Niall Brask equalised with a header from a corner six minutes after the break, before Verusan captain Halo Markenrick scored the winner in the 73rd minute with a long-range strike that deflected past Raledrian goalkeeper Joren Vahsk. The attendance of 88,950 was the highest of the tournament.<ref name="flla-final" />

==Statistics==

===Goalscoring===

[[Trian]] finished as the tournament's leading scoring nation with 12 goals across five matches, despite being eliminated in the quarter-finals, ahead of [[Taval]] (11) and a group of four sides level on 10.<ref name="flla-stats" /> The champions [[Verusa]] scored 10 goals across their six matches, the same total as the hosts [[Ukhdari]], [[Ohtina]] and [[Quidic]], the last of which failed to advance from the group stage.

===Discipline===

The FLLA Disciplinary Committee issued a total of 198 yellow cards and 11 red cards across the 64 matches of the tournament, an average of 3.09 yellows and 0.17 reds per match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/disciplinary-summary|title=1760 FLLA World Cup disciplinary summary|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=18 August 1760}}</ref> The most-cautioned team was [[Astye]], with 14 yellow cards across three matches; [[Raledria]] received the fewest among the four semi-finalists, with just four yellows and no reds across their seven matches, helping the team win the [[#Awards|FLLA Fair Play Trophy]]. Four players received red cards in the knockout stage: two in the round of sixteen, one in the quarter-finals and one in the third-place playoff.

==Awards==

The Best Player award, formally titled the FLLA Vairan Ball, was awarded by a panel of seven sports journalists drawn from each of the seven confederations to [[Verusa|Verusan]] central midfielder Halo Markenrick, who captained the champions throughout the tournament and contributed three goals and five assists across their six matches. Markenrick was the first Verusan player to win the award. [[Trian|Trianese]] forward Aldan Verric took the Marskval with seven personal strikes, the only player to reach seven in a tournament with no individual scorer in double figures.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/tournament-awards|title=Markenrick named best player as Verusa win 1760 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=11 July 1760}}</ref>

The Bastion, awarded to the tournament's best goalkeeper, went to Raledrian goalkeeper Joren Vahsk, who conceded only five goals and kept three clean sheets across his country's seven matches, including a 22-kick penalty shoot-out victory over [[Dahe]] in the round of sixteen. Verusan forward Devan Lehrek, 19 years old at the start of the tournament, was named Best Young Player after appearing in five of [[Verusa]]'s six matches and scoring the second goal in the semi-final against [[Ztesh]]. [[Raledria]] received the Fair Play award after finishing the tournament with the fewest disciplinary points of any of the four semi-finalists.

==Preparations and costs==

The total budget allocated to the 1760 FLLA World Cup by the Ukhdari Arraby Association and the Ukhdari federal government was {{lahn}}1.98&nbsp;billion. Of this, {{lahn}}1.22&nbsp;billion was directed towards stadium construction and renovation, {{lahn}}480&nbsp;million towards public-transport upgrades in the nine host cities, and {{lahn}}280&nbsp;million towards operational expenditure including security, broadcasting infrastructure and the volunteer programme. The transport allocation funded a new metro line in [[Faramozan]] (the Western Line, opened in April 1760) and a high-speed rail link between [[Veshgadar]] and [[Borshavi]] completed in February 1760. Per-venue capital costs averaged {{lahn}}163&nbsp;million across the ten stadiums, a figure later cited by FLLA reviewers as comparatively modest by the standards of the preceding three editions.<ref name="uaa-venues" />

Six of the ten venues, comprising Dy Sports Complex, Ezrum Coliseum, Hunzavir Arena, Hanzubek City Stadium, Ardashun Field and Tardakal Stadium, were either newly built or extensively redeveloped for the tournament. The newest, Hunzavir Arena, was inaugurated on 14 February 1760, four months before the opening match. Total stadium construction overran the original budget by 6&nbsp;per&nbsp;cent, primarily because of cost escalation at the Ardashun and Tardakal sites; the smaller per-venue capacities adopted in the bidding plan (none above 92,000 seats and the median venue at 56,500) limited the absolute scale of the overrun.

The Ukhdari security operation involved 28,000 police and military personnel deployed across the nine host cities, considerably below the figures recorded at later editions. No serious incidents were reported during the tournament.

Total tournament revenue, audited by the FLLA in August 1760, was {{lahn}}2.74&nbsp;billion, against costs of {{lahn}}1.98&nbsp;billion, yielding a net surplus of {{lahn}}760&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/financial-audit|title=1760 FLLA World Cup financial audit and revenue statement|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=22 August 1760}}</ref> The FLLA's standard 18&nbsp;per&nbsp;cent host-association allocation returned {{lahn}}493&nbsp;million to the Ukhdari Arraby Association, which was reinvested in domestic grassroots Arraby and youth development.

==Marketing==
{{Main|1760 FLLA World Cup marketing}}

The marketing programme for the 1760 FLLA World Cup was overseen by the Ukhdari Arraby Association in partnership with the FLLA's commercial division, with creative direction by the Faramozan-based studio Andan Mark. The programme included the official emblem, mascot, match ball and theme song (see [[#Symbols|Symbols]] below), a global travelling-trophy tour through 47 countries in the year preceding the tournament, and a tiered sponsorship structure of six worldwide partners, eight Ukhdari national partners and four regional supporters. Total sponsorship revenue across all three tiers was {{lahn}}1.18&nbsp;billion, the highest gross sponsorship figure recorded by any FLLA World Cup to date at the time of the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/commercial-programme|title=1760 FLLA World Cup commercial and sponsorship programme|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=30 August 1760}}</ref>

==Symbols==
{{Main|1760 FLLA World Cup symbols}}

===Emblem===

The official emblem of the tournament, designed by the Faramozan-based studio Andan Mark, was unveiled on 12 May 1757 in a public ceremony at the Ukhdari Museum of National History. The design depicts a stylised falcon, a long-standing motif in Ukhdari heraldry, holding the World Cup trophy in its talons, set against a circular crest in the Ukhdari national colours of blue, green, and gold. The emblem received the FLLA Council's formal endorsement in October 1757 after a four-week consultation period with member associations.

===Mascot===

The official mascot of the 1760 FLLA World Cup, named '''Falir''', is an anthropomorphic Ukhdari falcon dressed in the blue-green-and-gold colours of the host nation. The mascot was selected by a public vote organised by the Ukhdari Arraby Association in the spring of 1758, with three candidate designs presented to voters across the nine host cities and in print; Falir prevailed over a steppe-horse design ("Marasu") and a stylised wildflower ("Velina") with 49&nbsp;per&nbsp;cent of the 2.6 million votes cast.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1758/mascot-vote|title=Falir named official mascot of 1760 FLLA World Cup|publisher=Ukhdari Arraby Association|date=22 April 1758}}</ref>

===Match ball===

The official match ball, manufactured by the Ukhdari sports equipment maker Veska Sport, was branded the '''Sirana'''. The Sirana featured a traditional 32-panel hand-stitched construction in a green-and-gold polychrome livery, a presentation chosen to evoke the host nation's textile heritage. The ball was the last hand-stitched World Cup match ball before the thermally-bonded designs that followed at the [[1764 FLLA World Cup|1764 edition]]. A distinct gold-coloured version of the ball, the Sirana Final, was used in the final, the third-place playoff and the two semi-finals.

===Permanent trophy===

The permanent trophy of the 1760 FLLA World Cup, presented to the winners alongside the rotating [[FLLA World Cup#The Andah Cup|Andah Cup]] at the closing ceremony of the [[#Final|final]], was the '''Ardashun''', a 48-centimetre repoussé silver sculpture commissioned by the Ukhdari Arraby Association from the Faramozan-based studio Andan Mark, the same studio responsible for the [[#Emblem|tournament emblem]]. The work takes its name from the historic Ukhdari city of [[Ardashun]] and depicts a soaring falcon, the national animal of Ukhdari, in flight over a stylised mountain ridge representing the spine of the host nation. Hand-worked over an eight-month period at the studio's Faramozan workshop and finished in March 1760, the Ardashun was unveiled at the Ukhdari Museum of National History on 4 April 1760, eight weeks before the opening match. Following [[Verusa]]'s [[#Final|2–1 win]] over [[Raledria]], the trophy was transferred to permanent retention by the [[Verusa|Verusan]] federation and is displayed at the Verusan National Museum.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/permanent-trophy|title=The Ardashun unveiled as 1760 FLLA World Cup permanent trophy|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=4 April 1760}}</ref>

===Theme song===

The official theme song of the tournament, "One Field, One Game", was composed by Ukhdari musician Lariv Mokhan with lyrics jointly written by Mokhan and the vocalist Sava Reldan, who also performed the track. The studio recording was released on 1 April 1760 and topped the Ukhdari charts for seven consecutive weeks.

==Media==
{{Main|1760 FLLA World Cup broadcasting rights}}

The 1760 FLLA World Cup was broadcast in 166 countries by 51 official television partners and a further 22 official radio partners. Domestic broadcasting rights in [[Ukhdari]] were held by the Ukhdari National Broadcaster (UNB), which produced the host feed and screened all 64 matches across two of its terrestrial channels. The international rights for the [[AYFVL]] region were held by [[Verusa|Verusan]] public-service broadcaster VCN; the [[ATFVL]] rights by the [[Raledria|Raledrian]] National Network (RNN); and the [[ACFVL]] rights by a five-broadcaster consortium led by Estijan's national broadcaster ETP.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/broadcast-partners|title=Official broadcast partners of the 1760 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=1 May 1760}}</ref>

The final between [[Verusa]] and [[Raledria]] was the most-watched television broadcast in [[Verusa|Verusan]] history at the time, drawing a peak audience of 17.2 million viewers (representing approximately 88&nbsp;per&nbsp;cent of the active television audience in the country).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rnn.tv/1760/world-cup-final-ratings|title=1760 FLLA World Cup final sets Verusan viewing record|publisher=Raledrian National Network|date=13 July 1760}}</ref> Worldwide, the FLLA reported a cumulative live broadcast audience for the tournament of 3.1 billion individual viewers across all matches, with 1.5 billion individuals tuning in to at least part of the final.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/audience-summary|title=1760 FLLA World Cup viewership summary|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=18 August 1760}}</ref>

===Attendance===

Cumulative attendance across the 64 matches of the tournament was 3,178,856 spectators, an average of 49,670 per match.<ref name="flla-stats" /> The highest single-match attendance was the 88,950 recorded at the [[#Final|final]] in [[Faramozan]], just below the Stadion Faramozan's listed all-seater capacity of 92,000; the lowest was the 38,420 attending the Group H fixture between [[Dahe]] and [[Isari]] at the Ardashun Field on 20 June.

Across the tournament, attendance averaged 53,440 in the knockout stage and 47,910 in the group stage. The three matches involving the host nation drew the three highest group-stage attendances, with [[Ukhdari]] v [[Myla]] in Group F (89,100 at Stadion Faramozan) recording the largest group-stage crowd.

==Controversies==

The most prominent dispute of the tournament arose from the [[#Round of 16|round-of-sixteen]] tie between [[United Delet]] and [[Praesyu]] at the Ardashun Field on 30 June, in which Praesyu's 104th-minute extra-time winner, scored by Drasil, was allowed to stand despite United Delet protests that the ball had crossed the touchline in the build-up. United Delet television replays subsequently suggested the ball had left the field of play before the cross was delivered; the on-field officials, supported by the assistant referee on the near touchline, allowed the goal to stand. The Delet Arraby Association lodged a formal protest with the [[FLLA]] on 1 July seeking the result to be voided, which the FLLA Disciplinary Committee declined to entertain on 3 July, citing the finality of on-field decisions under the laws of the game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/united-delet-protest-ruling|title=FLLA Disciplinary Committee dismisses United Delet round-of-16 protest|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=3 July 1760}}</ref> An independent review of the broadcast footage published by the [[FLLA]] in September 1760 concluded that the original ruling had been "incorrect in isolation but consistent with the standards applied across the tournament".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flla.org/1760/officiating-review|title=Independent review of officiating at the 1760 FLLA World Cup|publisher=[[FLLA]]|date=18 September 1760}}</ref>

A separate complaint, lodged by the [[Praesyu|Praesyuan]] Arraby Association after the quarter-final defeat to [[Ztesh]], related to a substitution clarification request which had not been processed within the time agreed under the [[#Innovations|new written-slip procedure]]. The Praesyuan complaint was acknowledged but not upheld; the FLLA Council subsequently amended the substitution-slip rule for the [[1764 FLLA World Cup|1764 edition]] to require simultaneous oral and written confirmation.

==Aftermath==

[[Verusa]]'s victory was the second FLLA World Cup ever won by a Verusan side. The result was widely celebrated in Verusa, which had earlier in the year completed the constitutional reforms that established the country's current [[Verusa#History|Third Republic]]; the new federal government incorporated the team's homecoming parade into its programme of national celebration. The team returned to [[Huifarn]] on 13 July 1760 and was received by an estimated crowd of 2.9 million along a three-mile parade route from Huifarn's main airport station to the Federal Square.

In [[Ukhdari]], the tournament was judged a financial and operational success, even after the early elimination of the host side: an independent post-event report commissioned by the Ukhdari Arraby Association and published in October 1760 estimated the net economic contribution to the host economy at {{lahn}}5.1&nbsp;billion, against gross public expenditure of {{lahn}}1.98&nbsp;billion across infrastructure and operations.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.globaltradeunion.org/database/ukhdari-1760-event-impact|title=Economic impact of the 1760 FLLA World Cup on the Ukhdari economy|publisher=[[Global Trade Union]]|date=20 October 1760}}</ref> International visitor arrivals to Ukhdari over the tournament period totalled 820,000, the highest single-month visitor figure recorded by the Ukhdari Bureau of Tourism since the Bureau's creation in 1731.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gov.ukh/1760/uaa-impact-report|title=1760 FLLA World Cup post-event economic impact report|publisher=Ukhdari Arraby Association|date=14 October 1760}}</ref>

The next edition of the FLLA World Cup, the [[1764 FLLA World Cup]], was awarded to [[Raledria]] at the FLLA Council meeting of 12 March 1758, during the planning stage of the 1760 tournament. Verusa retained an automatic place at the 1764 finals under the reseeding rules adopted by the FLLA Council in 1761, which extended the long-standing host-qualifies exemption to the most recent champions; the 1761 reseeding rules were themselves influenced by the demonstration effect of Verusa's 1760 campaign, in which the eventual champions had qualified through a competitive AYFVL group stage and then advanced from the finals despite finishing second in their group.
